note: A tune that drops an octave, learned in named stages (with the tune, Tune muted, Chords muted), then a line of the singer's own over the 1st, 5th, 6th and 4th chords that holds a 4th, a 5th and an octave. The chords are tokens counted the long way, the old Key selector is now moves (any key, 60 to 90 bpm), and the line about another key is marked {{?key}}; the backing track keeps its distance a tone lower.

exercise.title: An octave tune, then every leap
exercise.why: From Do up to Sol is a 5th, from Sol up to the next Do is a 4th, and Do to Do is an octave, so three notes hold a 4th, a 5th and an octave.

cells.text:
Press Play below to hear the tune at {{=bpm}}: the mic starts with it. The tune starts on the high Do, drops an octave and dips under Do before it ends. Sing along on the note names.
Sing along with the tune a few times. Then press Tune below to mute the tune, and sing it over the chords alone.
Once the octave drop lands without a slide, press Chords to mute the chords too, and sing the tune a cappella.
{{?key}}In another key the notes change, but the drop is still an octave.

Press Start exercise below: the mic and the backing track start together. The backing track plays {{chord:I}}, {{chord:V}}, {{chord:vi}} and {{chord:IV}}, a bar each.
{{chord:I}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}, {{chord:V}} the 5th, built on {{5}}, {{chord:vi}} the 6th, built on {{6}}, and {{chord:IV}} the 4th, built on {{4}}. Make up a line from the ringed {{1}}, {{3}} and {{5}}, and put a 4th, a 5th and an octave somewhere in it. Sing it on "ah", and take the notes above the middle {{1}} on "oo".
Practice until each leap lands without a slide.
